title: Faithfully flat factorization of an affine group homomorphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G,H$ be affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:G\to H$ be a homomorphism. There exist an affine group scheme $I$ of finite type over $k$ and homomorphisms $u:G\to I$, $j:I\to H$ such that $f=j\circ u$, $j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $u$ is faithfully flat: $k[G]$ is a faithfully flat $k[I]$-module through $u^*:k[I]\to k[G]$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Here $k[X]=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for an affine $k$-scheme $X$. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, perfectness or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75 (homomorphism theorem for affine algebraic groups); its proof uses Proposition 3.14 for the finitely generated image Hopf algebra and Theorem 3.31 for faithful flatness of a Hopf subalgebra inclusion.

proof.text: Put $A=k[H]$, $B=k[G]$ and $\varphi=f^*:A\to B$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], both algebras have finite sets of $k$-algebra generators. Their coordinate Hopf maps satisfy the identities in [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. By [def-sc-group-scheme], $f$ is compatible with the multiplications, so on $R$-points it is a group homomorphism $G(R)\to H(R)$ for every $k$-algebra $R$; hence it also preserves identity and inverse on $R$-points, and therefore as morphisms (take $R=k$ for the identity, and the universal point $\mathrm{id}\in G(B)$ for the inverse). Pulling back these three compatibilities gives $\Delta_B\varphi=(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\Delta_A$, $\epsilon_B\varphi=\epsilon_A$, and $S_B\varphi=\varphi S_A$. Thus $\varphi$ is a homomorphism of commutative Hopf algebras.

source.place: Sections 3(b)--3(c), pp.65--67; Theorem 3.34, first sentence of proof, p.75.

proof.text: Let $C=\varphi(A)\subseteq B$, let $q:A\twoheadrightarrow C$ be corestriction, and let $i:C\hookrightarrow B$ be inclusion. This is a $k$-subalgebra and $\varphi=iq$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ generate $A$, every element of $C$ is a polynomial in $\varphi(a_1),\ldots,\varphi(a_r)$, so $C$ is finitely generated. For $c=\varphi(a)$ and $\Delta_A(a)=\sum a_s\otimes a^{\prime}_s$, step 1 gives $\Delta_B(c)=\sum\varphi(a_s)\otimes\varphi(a^{\prime}_s)\in C\otimes_k C$ and $S_B(c)=\varphi(S_A(a))\in C$. Restrict $\Delta_B,S_B,\epsilon_B$ to define $\Delta_C,S_C,\epsilon_C$. To justify this restriction and its axioms, extend a $k$-basis of the subspace $C$ to one of $B$ and let $r:B\to C$ be the linear projection with $ri=1_C$. Then $i^{\otimes n}$ has left inverse $r^{\otimes n}$ for $n=1,2,3$, hence is injective. The restricted comultiplication is therefore well defined independently of $a$ and its tensor presentation. Each algebra-map identity and each coassociative, counit or antipode identity becomes the corresponding identity for $B$ after applying the appropriate $i^{\otimes n}$, so holds in $C$. The same injectivity and the displayed formulas show that $q$ and $i$ preserve all three maps. This is the explicit image factorization of commutative Hopf algebras.

source.place: Definitions 3.8 and Proposition 3.9, p.67; Proposition 3.14, p.68; explicit restriction verification.

proof.text: Define $I=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $u=\operatorname{Spec}i$ and $j=\operatorname{Spec}q$, using the canonical identifications $G\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $H\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$. These canonical identifications commute with the group operations, since their pullbacks identify the multiplication, identity and inverse maps with the same coordinate maps of [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], $I$ is an affine $k$-group scheme, $u,j$ are group homomorphisms, and contravariant functoriality applied to $\varphi=iq$ gives $f=j\circ u$. The finite list of generators of $C$ gives the one-chart finite affine presentation required for $I\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to be of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $q$ is surjective, $\operatorname{Spec}q$ has affine preimage $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and its map on global sections is $q$, which is surjective; by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2), applied to the one-member affine cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and so is $j$, its composite with the isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\simeq H$.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, last sentence of proof, p.75; Proposition 3.6, p.66; affine closed-immersion criterion Stacks Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion-characterize.; Stacks Tag 01QO via lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion (2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-subalgebra-faithfully-flat] to the injective Hopf homomorphism $i:C\hookrightarrow B$. Both algebras are commutative and finitely generated over the same field $k$ by steps 1--2; the image Hopf identities give exactly its compatibility hypotheses. Hence $B$ is faithfully flat over $C$. As $u^*=i$, this is precisely the required faithful flatness of $k[G]$ over $k[I]$. All constructions used the image algebra, with its nilpotents retained, so impose none of the excluded smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, perfectness or characteristic assumptions.
